one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled binaries fall inside the window: NXP Q3 2026 results and Q4 guide on Oct 27 at 4:10 PM ET (first reaction Oct 28) and the FOMC decision on Oct 28 at 2:00 PM ET, after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% with more projected; TXN and STM report the week before. Alt-data points to an in-line-to-better print and a supportive Q4 guide: September trackers show allocation still tightening, not easing (Electronics Risk Brief Sep 2: automotive MCU prices up 15-20% cumulative in 2026; ST book-to-bill near 2 with distribution inventory below target; IC-Online sees no improvement before mid-2027), and NXP's third 2026 price round (~10% on select parts, effective Sep 28, single distributor source) lands in the Q4 guide. Against that: a hawkish Oct 28 FOMC would hit a cyclical multiple, and the market sold the last beat (Q2) on an in-line guide; recent earnings-week moves were +21% and -15%. Net I keep only a small upward tilt (median ~$237.5, ~0.4% above spot) with ~14% one-month log-vol (48%/3.5 plus an earnings/FOMC gap), i.e. P(>=spot) 0.51, essentially symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blend of 60% forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sept 2027 ~$19.0 x 14.0x = $266) and 40% FCF yield (2027 FCF ~$3.85B / 252M shares = ~$15.3/share at a 6.1% yield = $250), giving ~$260; multiple and yield tightened by ~25bp-equivalent for the confirmed Sep 16 Fed hike.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS as of Sept 2027 ~$19.0 x 14.0x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus 2027 $18.10 rolled forward ~3 quarters at ~8-10% growth. Upside from three 2026 NXP price rounds (Apr, Jun, ~10% Sep 28) and still-tightening September allocation is offset by double-ordering risk (peer ST book-to-bill ~2), China car retail -20.8% YTD against NXP China revenue +25% y/y (18% of sales), and modest 2027 auto production trims; I leave pricing upside to the bull case rather than the base EPS.

Stock is ~13.1x 2027 consensus today and was ~19x forward in June; the Fed's first hike since 2023 (Sep 16, more projected) caps re-rating, so I cut my round-1 14.5x to 14.0x, a small premium to today for 18-19% revenue growth.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027 revenue ~$16.0B x 24% FCF margin = $3.85B; 252.2M shares; 6.1% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 $3.18B + Q2 $3.50B (10-Q) + Q3 guide $3.75B + Q4 ~$3.9B assumed modest sequential growth helped by the Sep 28 price round.

~12% growth: pricing and SDV/industrial drivers offset flat-to-slightly-down 2027 vehicle builds (Mobility Global Sept update trims China -200k, Europe -100k, NA -70k units, small on ~90M) and China retail weakness.

Round-1 6.0% (above a ~4-5% mature analog peer for leverage and auto cyclicality) raised ~10bp for the confirmed Fed hike; the Ambarella risk is now treated as a small probability-weighted item (unconfirmed, ~5-6% of market cap) rather than a yield premium.

bear.story: The 2026 allocation/price-hike cycle (three NXP rounds, peer book-to-bill ~2) proves partly double-ordering; with China car retail down ~21% and channel inventory up to 11 weeks, H1 2027 brings an inventory correction and price give-backs; 2027 EPS ~$15, and a hiking Fed keeps the multiple ~11x. A cash Ambarella deal adds leverage worries.

base.story: Growth slows but holds: 2027 revenue ~+12%, EPS ~$18-19, pricing sticks on constrained parts, gross margin ~58-59%; the rate backdrop holds the multiple near 13.5-14x NTM.

bull.story: Tightness persists into mid-2027 as trackers expect; cumulative 2026 price rounds and VSMC 300mm volume production (Q1 2027) lift margins, 2027 EPS runs toward $20-21 and the stock regains ~17x, retesting the $340 high.

thesis_break_reason: Below the $183 52-week low and ~9.7x the $18.10 2027 consensus. Trading there would most likely mean the market is pricing a genuine 2027 earnings reset: the 2026 allocation/pricing cycle unwinding as double-ordering (the key alt-data tell would be distributor lead times shortening and price notices stopping), a China/channel correction, or a rate-driven cyclical de-rating plus a value-destroying acquisition, rather than ordinary 47-48% vol noise.

key_uncertainties: Whether 2026 allocation and three price rounds reflect real end demand or precautionary double-ordering that unwinds in 2027 (September trackers still show tightening, which is the late-cycle pattern)
Fed path after the Sep 16 hike and its effect on cyclical semiconductor multiples

reasoning: Round 2. Facts unchanged: Q2 2026 revenue $3.50B (+19% y/y), EPS $3.61, Q3 guide $3.75B/$4.11, FCF 23% of revenue, net debt $7.7B, 252M shares, 2027 consensus EPS $18.10 (13.1x at $236). Supervisor findings I adopt: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 with the next FOMC on Oct 28 (I had no macro driver), so I cut the P/E to 14.0x and raise the FCF yield to 6.1%; the Mobility Global cuts are small (-200k China, -100k Europe, -70k NA for 2027), so I soften that point, but China car retail -20.8% YTD vs NXP China +25% y/y is a bounded bear point that fattens the left tail; Ambarella is unconfirmed and small, so it no longer sets a yield premium; I now cite the FT/Yahoo original rather than the X relay. On the supervisor's ask about data freshness: my round-1 trackers were April-June; September sources (Electronics Risk Brief Sep 2, TrendForce Aug 21, IC-Online Aug 14) show allocation still tightening, auto MCU prices +15-20% YTD, ST book-to-bill near 2, and a third NXP price round (~10%, effective Sep 28; single distributor source, so labelled judgment-grade and kept out of base EPS). That is near-term positive (Q4 guide) but is also the classic late-cycle double-ordering signature, so it raises both tails rather than the median. Fair value falls from $267 to $260 (P/E $266, FCF $250). Scenarios: bear $168 (27%), base $257 (48%), bull $342 (25%). Ladder is a three-lognormal mixture (widths 0.32/0.28/0.30), effective log-sd ~0.39, median ~$251, mean ~$266; I widened from round 1 (~0.33) toward, but not all the way to, the 47% realized vol because the realized figure is inflated by one V-shaped cycle swing ($191->$340->$229) and 12-month dispersion for a large-cap is usually lower than annualized weekly vol. P(>=spot) drops from 0.60 to 0.56 for the rate headwind. 1-month ladder is near-symmetric (median ~$237.5, sigma ~14%) with earnings and FOMC in the window. Research this round: 7 searches/fetches.
